title: Python conversational proxy: ackable events, resume-safe iterator, and telemetry contract
creator: Miguel Romero
description: Create a high-level conversational proxy in the Python SDK that presents a single ergonomic API for streaming chat completions while surfacing typed events (partial tokens, role changes, structured tool calls, system signals) and explicit ack/nack semantics. The proxy should make it straightforward for application code to: resume after intermittent connection loss, perform idempotent retries for individual messages, emit stable telemetry hooks (latency/cost per-message, ack lag), and provide a small set of primitives for backpressure and graceful shutdown. This ticket covers design + prototype + initial implementation and tests for the core primitives and example recipes.
acceptance_criteria: ConversationProxy exists as a runtime class in redwood_sdk.conversation with an async iterator that yields typed events (TokenDelta, SegmentBoundary, ToolCall, Finalization, AckSignal)
Proxy supports explicit ack() / nack(reason) calls per message segment and exposes a small signal bus for application-level signals (pause/resume/cancel)

Resume behavior: after a transient disconnect, a new client can call proxy.resume(checkpoint_token) and receive a deterministic stream from the last acknowledged boundary without duplicate final messages
Retry semantics documented and implemented: safe at-most-once finalization for non-ack'd segments and at-least-once for idempotent tool calls when opted-in
Telemetry hooks: per-segment metrics emitted (emit_metric API) and an example dashboard link included in the design doc
Comprehensive unit + integration tests including a fault-injection harness that simulates partial writes, delayed acks, and reorder events
Examples: two cookbook examples (graceful-shutdown recipe and resumable-conversation recipe) added to examples/ and referenced from README
PR reviewed and merged with accompanying docs and changelog entry
implementation_notes: API shape: ConversationProxy(stream_generator, checkpoint_store, telemetry_emitter, retry_policy)
Internals: adapter layer converts raw SSE/HTTP2 events into a small typed event enum in Python; maintain a checkpoint object that contains last_ack_boundary, kv_cache_snapshot_id, and token_offset
Checkpoint token must be compact and opaque (base64 JSON) to avoid coupling; include version field for future format evolution
Ack semantics: ack() advances last_ack_boundary and persists to checkpoint_store asynchronously; implement best-effort batching of checkpoint writes to avoid excessive IO
Backpressure primitive: proxy.pause_consumption() / proxy.resume_consumption() that coordinates with underlying read buffer and exposes a max_pending_tokens counter
Failure modes: network partitions -> proxy exposes partial_finish(reason) event; on resume clients must rehydrate the local conversation tape and call resume(checkpoint_token)
Compatibility: provide a compatibility shim for legacy sync iterator API to avoid breaking existing users
Security: checkpoint token should not embed PII; use deterministic hashing for any identifiers
test_plan: Unit tests for event demux: TokenDelta -> text assembly / boundary detection
Integration test using local_fault_harness: simulate TCP drop mid-segment and verify resume semantics with persisted checkpoint
Property tests for checkpoint token roundtrip and forward-compatibility with a rotated format version
Load test: exercise pause/resume under sustained 400 tps chat messages and ensure no more than 2% token duplication observed
End-to-end example tests included in CI that run the two cookbook scripts and assert expected final message contents and telemetry emission
